chunks: And by this chain, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Ismail al-Sufi, from al-Abbas ibn Abi al-Abbas, from Abdus ibn Ibrahim al-Baghdadi, who raised the narration to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He said: Henna removes the dullness (of the skin), increases the moisture of the face, improves the scent, and beautifies the offspring. And he said: One who applies henna and rubs it from the root of the hair to the foot, poverty will be removed from him.

key_terms.السَّهَكِ: Dullness or lack of luster in the skin
key_terms.الْحِنَّاءُ: Henna, a natural dye used for hair and skin
key_terms.مَاءِ الْوَجْهِ: Moisture or freshness of the face

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and physical benefits of applying henna according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the spiritual and physical virtues of henna, linking its aesthetic benefits—such as removing dullness and beautifying offspring—to the removal of poverty (*al-faqr*). The promise of financial relief is specifically tied to the comprehensive application of henna from the hair roots to the feet, reflecting the Shia emphasis on integrating bodily care with divine reward.
